reason: r18 is the insertion build, unchanged from r17 except the gate that stopped r17's run: the cache sizing field at row+8 is the tree's node count (the r17 run read 3 objects against 3 tree nodes), while the row's object array is that count plus one (its first entry is the controller), and r17 required the former to equal the latter. The insertion puts one cGUIObjScissorMask into the gauge row under the row's root, over the bar, glow and edge, writes the sharpness-ratio clip box into the mask's built rectangle (+0xb0..+0xbc) from the draw walker with bit 1 of +0xa4 kept clear, grows the object array from 4 words to 5 through the cGUIInstance DTI's MT allocator (MtDti::getAllocator, main+0x7aa47c) publishing instance+0xd8 and root+0xa0, and reallocates the row's draw block through the root's vtable slot 0x58 with main+0xa49b28's arithmetic, freeing the old blocks. The r17 run of 2026-10-24 (NRO 626d96f75fe9102febf30d9c09a2b38714fddcb943ca6e55465ab50c3c1f6749, 95 plugin lines, installed bytes matching) is the evidence for the rule and for the row's geometry: counts8 0x00100003 = 3 objects and 16 sequences, published cache 192 = 16*12 into the allocation, so the record area is (3 << 4) | 8 = 56 bytes = 7 records and the inserted tree's 9 records are 16 bytes past the end - r14 overflowed the draw records and desynchronised the map, and an insertion has to grow both. The insertion itself wrote nothing in that run, and the user saw the gauge unchanged. r14 (NRO 6e061c70779cfb3a306835030256012e50dd19fdbeeae36d4d4635c331d35b8d) remains the failed insertion run: the rectangle the game built from the mask had left/top 0 0 in all 2512 lines, never the requested 110,32, and main+0x5456e4 indexes the instance's array by the tree's node count + 1. r16 (NRO 415a822a2d3643efc1b5704c1e84814200be593c7922d297e85f535991acc0ed) ran clean with the map read out. Not approved for distribution; r12 and r13 were packaged and never run.
runtime_test: NOT RUN: r18 is r17's insertion with the stage-48 gate comparison corrected (objects == tree_nodes, the map staying at nodes + 1). r17 ran once on Eden 2026-10-24 (installed bytes 626d96f75fe9102febf30d9c09a2b38714fddcb943ca6e55465ab50c3c1f6749, 95 plugin lines, insertion stopped by its own gate at stage 48, gauge reported normal, zero guest exceptions, session closed normally); r16 ran clean on Eden 2026-10-23; r14 ran once and failed as reported.

limitations: r4 has no runtime test; its lines, the 320-sample budget and the absence of any drawing change are static results.
r2 was built and never run; r3 was run once on Eden and is recorded.
r14 was run once on Eden and failed as reported: the gauge was clipped away from the insertion and the game crashed at the quest end. Its log is the evidence, and the insertion is removed in r15.

r15 was run once on Eden and drew the gauge normally for 740 seconds with no exception; its facts line printed tree_nodes 3 against 4 objects, and its object-list fields were read from the wrong object (the controller's owner field), which is what r16 fixes.

r16 changes nothing on screen: it reads game memory and logs. No drawing, no gauge change, and no cleanup claim (the root-destructor hook fired zero times in the three sessions that logged it). Its Eden run ended in Eden's own shutdown records (maxwell_3d Critical asserts, ForceStop, host SIGSEGV) with zero guest exceptions.
the game's destructor is assumed to free the map block r17 publishes through the cGUIInstance DTI's MT allocator; that free has not been observed, and r17 frees the old 4-word block itself
The per-weapon tier tables live in RomFS weapon data and are not read in this workspace: no weapon data file is extracted here.
The gauge itself is not part of r4.

r18 has not been run, and no build of this mod has completed an insertion: r14's ran and failed (the gauge clipped away, crash at the quest end), r17's stopped at its own stage-48 gate and wrote nothing. The mask construction, the grown map, the reallocated draw block (root vtable slots 0x58/0x5c) and the per-frame rectangle write at mask+0xb0..+0xbc are all without runtime evidence, and the mask's teardown is unproven, the root-destructor hook having fired zero times in the five sessions that logged it
